entities.summary:
Margherita Guarducci was an Italian archaeologist, classical scholar, and epigrapher. She was a major figure in several crucial moments of the 20th-century academic community. A student of Federico Halbherr, she edited his works after his death. She was the first woman to lead archaeological excavations at the Vatican, succeeding Ludwig Kaas, and completed the excavations on Saint Peter's tomb, identifying finds as relics of Saint Peter.

She also engaged in discussions on the authenticity of the Praeneste fibula, arguing that its inscription is a forgery. Margherita Guarducci was a journalists & chroniclers from Florence (1902-12-20, Florence–1999-09-02). A moderately significant entity in the historical record. Relevant to cause-and-effect analysis.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Margherita Guarducci's excavations at the Vatican and her identification of relics as those of Saint Peter had significant regional impact on the Catholic Church and its practices. Her work also shed light on the Praeneste fibula inscription, contributing to a better understanding of ancient Roman artifacts.
